### TAG-227: `Emitter: entry-invocation mutex-group arguments aren't unwrapped into member ports`

**Status:** ⬜ Not started

## Software Notes

When a top-level entry invocation supplies a \*\*brace group\*\* (mutex, \`{...}\`) as a source argument, the emitter can't unwrap the group into its member places. Instead it emits the literal string \`{mutex}\` as the argument's "text", fails to parse that as anything, and ties the DUT input to \`null_value\`. The group members are never emitted as ports and never wired through.

Reproduced with TAG-147:

fanin($selin1 {$outA1 $outB1})(dest1<>)

```
The emitted `fanin_network` in `.verify_scratch/TAG-147-example-12.13.ms.ipl.vhd`:
```vhdl
entity fanin_network is
  port(
    dest1 : out ncl_signal
  );
end fanin_network;
architecture rtl of fanin_network is
  signal arg_0 : ncl_signal;
  signal arg_1 : ncl_signal;
  signal arg_2 : ncl_signal;
begin
  -- TODO: non-literal entry argument 'selin1' not yet supported
  arg_0 <= null_value;
  -- TODO: non-literal entry argument '{mutex}' not yet supported
  arg_1 <= null_value;
  -- entry invocation supplied fewer arguments than the DUT has inputs
  arg_2 <= null_value;
  dut : entity work.fanin port map (
    ms_select => arg_0,
    in1 => arg_1,
    in2 => arg_2,
    ms_out => dest1
  );
end rtl;
```

The second source argument is a mutex group `{$outA1 $outB1}`. It should be unwrapped into two positional inputs — `outA1` and `outB1` — matching the DUT's `fanin` entity's two group-member ports (`in1`, `in2`). Instead it's collapsed to the literal string `{mutex}` and tied to `null_value`, while the padding loop separately fills the second group-member slot with `arg_2 <= null_value`. The two members of the group end up indistinguishable from placeholder padding.
Same shape across all five `fanin_network*` entities.

## Where the current behavior lives

Two functions are involved, and they're both wrong for this case.
`invocation.zig`**'s** `argToText` — returns the literal string `"{mutex}"` for a mutex-kind group:

```zig
pub fn argToText(arg: network.Arg) []const u8 {
    return switch (arg.kind) {
        .place => if (arg.name.len > 0) arg.name else arg.text,
        .literal, .expression => arg.text,
        .group => if (arg.group) |g| switch (g.kind) {
            .bundle => "[group]",
            .mutex => "{mutex}",
            .arbitration => "{{arbitration}}",
        } else "",
    };
}
```

That string is meaningful only as a diagnostic label, not as a piece of data the emitter can use.
`network_entity.zig`**'s entry-argument loop** — calls `argToText`, tries `parseInt`, fails, emits a TODO comment and `null_value`:

```zig
for (entry.sources, 0..) |arg, i| {
    const text = invocation.argToText(arg);
    const trimmed = std.mem.trim(u8, text, " \t\r\n");
    const value = std.fmt.parseInt(u64, trimmed, 10) catch {
        try writer.print("  -- TODO: non-literal entry argument '{s}' not yet supported\n", .{trimmed});
        try writer.print("  arg_{d} <= null_value;\n", .{i});
        continue;
    };
    try writer.print("  arg_{d} <= data_value({d});\n", .{ i, value });
}
```

Same loop is the subject of the separate place-name ticket; this ticket is specifically the group case.
**The padding loop** then fills in what it thinks are missing arguments:

```zig
if (dut_source_count > entry.sources.len) {
    try writer.print("  -- entry invocation supplied fewer arguments than the DUT has inputs\n", .{});
    for (entry.sources.len..dut_source_count) |i| {
        try writer.print("  arg_{d} <= null_value;\n", .{i});
    }
}
```

Because `entry.sources.len` counts the *group* as one argument, and `dut_source_count` counts the DUT's flattened inputs, the arithmetic is off by (group_size - 1) whenever a group is present. For a two-member group: `entry.sources.len == 2` (one `selin1`, one group), `dut_source_count == 3` (three DUT inputs: `ms_select`, `in1`, `in2`), so the loop adds one placeholder. But the correct allocation is `selin1 → ms_select`, group member 0 → `in1`, group member 1 → `in2` — three filled slots, zero placeholders.

## What the fix needs to do

**Unwrap the group argument into its members positionally.** For `fanin($selin1 {$outA1 $outB1})(dest1<>)`:

* Argument 0 is a place `selin1` → binds to DUT input 0 (`ms_select`).
* Argument 1 is a mutex group with members `outA1`, `outB1` → binds to DUT inputs 1 and 2 (`in1`, `in2`), in order.
  The `arg_N` signal allocation needs to be aware of this — the loop's `i` index must advance by the number of DUT slots an argument occupies, not by one per argument.
  **Emit input ports for each group member.** Same requirement as the place-name ticket: `outA1` and `outB1` need to become input ports on `fanin_network` so the entity can be driven. This overlaps with the place-name ticket's port-emission change; whichever lands first should leave a structure the other can use.
  **Drive** `arg_N` **from the member ports.** For each group member, emit `arg_N <= <member_port>;` rather than `arg_N <= null_value;`.
  **Reconcile the padding arithmetic.** With groups unwrapped before `dut_source_count` is compared, the comparison should be between the number of *flattened DUT slots* and the number of *flattened entry arguments*. Something like:

```zig
var entry_slot_count: usize = 0;
for (entry.sources) |arg| {
    entry_slot_count += boundary.boundaryCount(&.{arg});
}
```

Then the padding loop pads from `entry_slot_count..dut_source_count` — which is zero for a correctly-specified entry like TAG-147's, and positive only when the entry genuinely supplies fewer arguments than the DUT has inputs.
**Nested groups.** A group whose members are themselves groups is not exercised by any current example, and the code can fail loudly (`error.NestedGroupInvocationNotSupported`) the way `writeInvocationArgumentMember` already does. The fix for flat groups is enough for [TAG-147](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-147/example-1213-parallel-bus).

## Acceptance criteria

* TAG-147's `fanin_network*` entities have input ports for `selinN`, `outAN`, and `outBN` (sanitized). The DUT's `ms_select`, `in1`, `in2` receive values driven from those ports, not from `null_value`.
* The emitted `fanin_network` architecture contains three `arg_N` signals, all driven from ports or literals, with no `null_value` placeholders.
* No spurious "entry invocation supplied fewer arguments than the DUT has inputs" comment for a correctly-specified entry.
* `fanout_network` (whose entry arguments are places, not groups) is unaffected by this ticket — that's the place-name ticket.
* No regression on `zig verify`'s GHDL column.

## Scope notes

* This ticket and the place-name ticket both modify `writeOneNetworkEntity`'s entry-argument loop. They should probably be implemented together, or at least the same PR, because the loop needs a coherent structure to handle both "argument is a place name" and "argument is a group of place names" and "argument is a literal". Splitting them into two independent fixes risks one landing and breaking the other.
* The `argToText` helper in `invocation.zig` returns diagnostic strings (`"{mutex}"`) that are useful for error messages but must not be used as data. The fix should stop calling it from the entry-argument path and either use the group's member list directly or add a new helper that walks the group.
* The mutex-vs-bundle-vs-arbitration distinction in `group.kind` doesn't matter for the emitter here — all three are "N source slots supplied as one argument". The emitter can treat them uniformly for positional binding. Semantic differences (mutex = exactly one valid, bundle = all valid, arbitration = priority) are the runtime's concern, not the port-map emitter's.
* The DUT's own side (`writeNetworkSourceMapping`) already walks `matched.sources` and recurses into groups, allocating `arg_N` per flattened slot. The entry side needs to match that flattening. The two are currently asymmetric: DUT flattens, entry doesn't. Restoring symmetry is the essence of this fix.

## Related

* [TAG-147](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-147/example-1213-parallel-bus) — the example that surfaces this
* The place-name ticket — sibling fix in the same function; the two should land together
* `writeInvocationArgument` / `writeInvocationArgumentMember` in `invocation.zig` — the *invocation site inside a definition* already handles group arguments correctly (see the earlier `fanin`/`fanout` invocations inside `bus` in [TAG-180](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-180/example-1210-conditional-input-expression)), and can serve as the model for how the entry-invocation emitter should flatten a group
* The contained-dispatch-cases ticket — separate, but same file
